blockers.description: HUMANKIND native install throughput is well below the official Steam client's (spot-checked: 489 Mbps / ~5min under real Steam vs ~4-12 MiB/s / rising latency under GameLib, even after the concurrency fix landed). Root cause NOT yet found. Ruled out: undici's default per-origin connection pool is unbounded (verified by reading node_modules/undici/lib/dispatcher/pool.js directly), so this is not an HTTP connection-reuse cap. Two live hypotheses, neither confirmed: (a) InflightLimiter only wraps the network fetch phase, so workers mid-decode/mid-disk-write don't count toward the 32 budget, naturally under-utilizing it; (b) genuine capacity/congestion on the 3 regional SteamCache nodes that won host selection fairly (lowest weightedload) over the generic CDN edges.
blockers.workaround: None applied. Options for the resuming session: (1) accept current throughput as sufficient since it does NOT stall/fail, and let a full HUMANKIND install run to completion to get Gate 2's actual data, or (2) open a proper debug session (packet capture / compare request pattern against the official client) to chase the remaining throughput gap before re-attempting Gate 2.
